title: Japan Rising - JX 1.1 ALPHA 2 R13.1
desc:
Japan enters 1933 with a powerful fleet, limited industrial resources and competing demands from the Army and Navy. Invest in factories, shipping, training and reserves to prepare for conflict in China and across the Pacific. Choose Japan's future alliances and peace terms from the position we build.

Garrisons defend local bases, Mountain Infantry handle difficult terrain and Marines lead opposed landings. Production priorities and regional agreements can support the forces you build.

title: Sarawak: the agreement needs attention
desc: Our envoys cannot yet confirm the agreed government, access or Japanese bases. Continue negotiations in 30 days at no additional cost, or retain the present position. Territory already ceded remains with its present owner.

title: Sarawak builds a defence force
desc: Local recruits form three infantry divisions at half strength. They require reinforcement and supplies. An existing army of six or more divisions receives no duplicate formation reserve.

commands: type = trigger which = 28601204

title: A settlement for Thailand
desc:
Thailand can no longer hold its main centres. A puppet joins Japan's wars and rebuilds local forces. A neutral treaty state stays outside our alliance and grants access.

A base treaty reserves only listed ports already held by Japan: no reserved ports. Other land returns to the local government. This settlement does not end Japan's other wars.

Consider these terms when ready, or retain the present occupation.

title: A settlement for Indonesia
desc:
Indonesia can no longer hold its main centres. A puppet joins Japan's wars and rebuilds local forces. A neutral treaty state stays outside our alliance and grants access.

A base treaty reserves only listed ports already held by Japan: Soerabaja (1653). Other land returns to the local government. This settlement does not end Japan's other wars.

Consider these terms when ready, or retain the present occupation.

title: Can America accept a Pacific armistice?
desc:
After two years of war, secure Hawaii, Singapore and the Philippines and maintain a credible carrier force. America must also have lost substantial carrier strength. Hold that position for six months before terms are offered.

This is an Allied-Pacific armistice: Britain and other Allied members also leave the war against Japan's bloc. Germany's separate European war continues. Japan must remain outside Germany's alliance. Overseas land outside the named Asian settlement returns to its legal owner.

purpose: Builder supplies the exact checked Asian/island province list. Only owned land currently controlled by Japan transfers.

title: The Allied-Pacific war ends
desc: The Allied powers and Japan's bloc accept the stated Pacific armistice. The European war and any separate Japanese-Soviet war continue. The treaty does not annex the United States or transfer its surviving army.

actions.name: Sign the Pacific armistice
commands: type = peace which = JAP value = 0
type = non_aggression which = USA where = JAP when = 1800
type = event which = 28600475 where = JAP when = 2
actions.gate: NOT = { alliance = { country = JAP country = GER } }

title: The Pacific settlement is in force
desc: The Allied-Pacific war has ended. Japan retains the territories named in the settlement and its existing partners. The German and Soviet wars are governed by their separate diplomatic state. Reconstruction and later treaty choices remain available through 1950.

actions.name: Begin the next chapter
commands: type = setflag which = JX_US_PEACE
type = clrflag which = JX_US_PENDING
type = dissent value = -2
type = event which = 28600476 where = JAP when = 1800
actions.gate: NOT = { war = { country = JAP country = USA } }

actions.name: The ceasefire failed; reopen negotiations
commands: type = clrflag which = JX_US_PENDING
type = setflag which = JX_US_WAIT
type = event which = 28600464 where = JAP when = 30
actions.gate: war = { country = JAP country = USA }

title: The Pacific treaty approaches its end
desc: The five-year non-aggression period is ending. Renew it, or allow ordinary diplomacy to resume. Letting a treaty expire does not automatically declare war.

actions.name: Renew the non-aggression agreement
commands: type = non_aggression which = JAP where = USA when = 1800

actions.name: Let ordinary diplomacy resume
commands: type = setflag which = JX_US_TREATY_EXPIRED

title: Demand terms after an American defeat
desc: From 1943, America must have lost 40 percent of its national provinces and Japan must hold San Diego, Los Angeles, San Francisco or Seattle. title: Call up the island defence detachments
desc:
Put 21 small, local detachments on Taiwan, Okinawa, Amami and the Japanese Pacific islands. Each is capped at 25 percent of a full garrison division and has no artillery brigade. Mobilisation cannot expand it beyond that cap.

The call-up costs 53 manpower, 900 supplies and 60 money, once. These local defenders can resist an empty-base raid; they cannot replace a fleet or stop a supported invasion. The first local-defence call-up also transfers 180 convoy transports and 90 convoy escorts to the national shipping pool, once across all these call-ups. They support island supply; they are not troop-transport flotillas or combat destroyers. Route allocation remains under convoy management.

desc: Long-range land-based naval bombers retain full naval striking power. They cost less to construct but use more fuel and are more vulnerable than standard naval bombers. Flying boats remain better maritime search aircraft. One initially recruited formation joins at an operational Japanese home airfield. Its equipment uses the latest researched model whose service year has arrived. The first formation is already funded and recruited: this issue takes no money, manpower or supplies from the national pool. Further formations require normal production, crews and maintenance. If no listed home base is usable, the issue waits until one is ready.
